subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw support non-thread persistent native and ACP `sessions_spawn` sessions as a first-class contract, and what routing and lifecycle semantics should that contract use?
rationale: The source-level limitation is clear, but accepting the requested behavior changes session ownership, parent delivery, thread bypass behavior, ACP inline delivery, cleanup, and follow-up targeting policy.

options.title: Define non-thread persistence
options.body: Approve an explicit unbound persistent-session contract and require one coordinated implementation across runtime, schema, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep session thread-bound
options.body: Keep `mode="session"` tied to thread binding and narrow this issue toward docs, current-conversation bindings, or `mode="run"` guidance.

options.title: Split ACP from native sessions
options.body: Handle ACP non-thread persistence through a separate affinity-style contract while deciding native subagent persistence later.

recommendation.title: Define non-thread persistence
recommendation.body: Approve an explicit unbound persistent-session contract and require one coordinated implementation across runtime, schema, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent core thread-binding ownership work makes this the best available routing owner for the product-contract decision.
